inputs.name: public_url
inputs.description: The address people reach Passbolt at, such as "https://passbolt.example.com". Passbolt builds every link from it and checks it at each sign-in, so it must be the address in the browser. Use https: the browser extension expects it.

inputs.name: admin
inputs.description: The first admin to register, such as { email = "you@example.com", first_name = "Sam", last_name = "Rivera" }. The first apply writes their invitation link to /etc/passbolt/admin-invite.txt on the host. When null, register one yourself, as the README shows.

inputs.name: server_key_email
inputs.description: Email address on the OpenPGP key Passbolt makes for itself on its first start. When null, passbolt@ and the host of public_url.

inputs.name: passbolt_version
inputs.description: Tag of the docker.io/passbolt/passbolt image, such as "5.17.0-1-ce-non-root". Only the ce-non-root images fit: they serve on port 8080 as an ordinary user. Change image_digest with it.

inputs.name: image_digest
inputs.description: Digest of docker.io/passbolt/passbolt for passbolt_version. Podman pulls by the digest, so a tag that moves upstream can't change what runs.

inputs.name: mariadb_version
inputs.description: Tag of the docker.io/library/mariadb image for Passbolt's database, such as "10.11.19". 10.11 is the series Passbolt's own Compose file uses. Change mariadb_digest with it.

inputs.name: listen_address
inputs.description: Address Passbolt listens on for plain HTTP. The default keeps it on the host, for a reverse proxy with TLS in front.

inputs.name: environment
inputs.description: More of Passbolt's environment variables, such as { EMAIL_TRANSPORT_DEFAULT_HOST = "smtp.example.com", EMAIL_TRANSPORT_DEFAULT_PASSWORD = "..." }. They go in a root-only env file and never reach the plan or state.
